summary: In-place title-case conversion of a NUL-terminated byte string. Capitalizes the first character if it is lowercase (this[0] in 97..122, subtract 32), then walks from this[1] and, for each character, inspects the previous character: if the previous character is a non-letter (outside 'a'-'z' and 'A'-'Z') the current character is uppercased when lowercase, otherwise the current character is lowercased when uppercase. Other characters pass through unchanged. Returns the trailing NUL byte. Called by SettingsCopySetupFileCopy (00432220).

local_names.v5: current character on the letter-predecessor branch
local_names.v7: current character on the non-letter-predecessor branch

operations.description: Guard 0: if *this (this+0x0) is >= 97 ('a') it may be a lowercase letter; combined with the upper bound 122 ('z') the first character is lowercase.
Capitalize the first character in place: *this = v1 - 32 (ASCII case delta).
Iterate from i = this + 1 while the current character (*i) is non-zero; the result value tracks the current character.
Guards 1 and 2: read the previous character v4 = *(i - 1); it is a non-letter when v4 < 97 (not a lowercase letter) and v4 < 65 (not any letter), i.e. outside 'A'-'Z' and 'a'-'z'.
Non-letter predecessor branch: if the current character *i is not in 97..122 ('a'-'z', lowercase) skip it; otherwise it is a lowercase letter to be capitalized.
Uppercase a lowercase current character: *i = v7 - 32.
Letter predecessor branch: if the current character *i is not in 65..90 ('A'-'Z', uppercase) skip it; otherwise it is an uppercase letter to be decapitalized.
Lowercase an uppercase current character: *i = v5 + 32.
Return the trailing NUL byte (result = this[1] initially, updated to *++i as the loop advances); the return value is not used for case conversion.

unresolved: Guard literals are ASCII constants from the raw source (97/'a', 122/'z', 65/'A', 90/'Z', delta 32); the case-mask reading (0x20) is not used because no such hex literal is evidenced in the packet.
The caller context (SettingsCopySetupFileCopy 0x00432220) suggests the converted string is a settings or copy-file description, but no class ownership is evidenced.
The guard table encodes the previous-character checks on the this+0x1 field representative; the loop actually reads *(i-1) relative to the cursor, which may be any position in the string.
The return value (trailing NUL) is an artifact of the loop test, not a deliberate result contract.
